testPolicy.text: Test scores are optional. Students who submit them must send official scores from the testing agencies (self-reported scores are not accepted); USC superscores the SAT and ACT by section. The admissions page refers to 'our test-optional policy'.

facts.text: Students from U.S. families earning $80,000 a year or less with typical assets attend USC tuition free.
The 2026-27 on-campus cost of attendance is $103,162 (tuition $75,384), up from $99,139 in 2025-26, plus a $450 new student fee in the first semester.
For fall 2025, of 9,345 admitted first-years, 3,692 were California residents, 3,378 out-of-state and 2,275 international; of 3,759 who enrolled, 1,701 were from California.

Early Decision (November 1) is binding and open to most majors, alongside non-binding, non-restrictive Early Action on the same date; dance, drama and music applicants (Kaufman, Dramatic Arts, Thornton) can only apply Regular Decision by December 1.
The World Bachelor in Business program in the Marshall School accepts applications only by the November 1 deadline and no longer takes Regular Decision applicants.
Testing is optional: only 33 percent of the fall 2025 enrolled class submitted SAT scores and 12 percent ACT scores, so the published score ranges describe a minority of students.

notes: CDS 2025-26 posted October 2026 (inner page headers still read 'Common Data Set 2024-2025', but C1 states Fall 2025). C1 totals: applied 37,036 men + 46,419 women + 33 unknown; admitted 4,580 + 4,759 + 6; enrolled 1,745 + 2,013 + 1. CDS G1 lists 2026-27 tuition as $66,640 and required fees $2,047, which contradicts the financial aid office's 2026-27 tuition of $75,384 and fees $1,952; the financial aid office figures were used. CDS C21 answers 'No' to Early Decision for the fall 2025 cohort while the current admissions page offers binding ED; the admissions page was used for the 2026-27 plans. CDS H2 (2025-26 aid year) shows first-years whose need was met at 99.4 percent on average, but USC does not publish a '100 percent of need' promise on the pages opened. No official fall 2026 (Class of 2030) figures found on usc.edu; consultant blogs quote 79,290 applicants and 9,251 admits but were not used. Test-optional start date not found on an official page opened. Web search quota ran out during this batch, so further official pages could not be searched for.
